parts:
Hi,
You can read the file as a data.frame make sure the format is the same as the internal format of methylKit, use stringsAsFactors=FALSE, when reading, also make sure other data slots are correct and consistent for all the files. You have to create a new methylRaw object with the new() function. an example is here:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/methylkit_discussion/new(%22methylRaw%22/methylkit_discussion/ndnXcLSBvLA/ezQHO3c0ZywJ

Then you can make a new methylRawList object,example is below:
# this creates a methlyRawList object from two methylRaw objects so the treatment vector has two elements.
# You can create a list with more elements
methylRawList=new("methylRawList",list(methylRawobj1,methylRawobj2),treatment=c(0,1 ) )

reading data faster
I recently created an experimental function mread, that should read large files faster, but it will not help with the memory. You can give it a try:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/methylkit_discussion/na3jqfCgD1A/A440aOTHhHkJ

Best,
Altuna

On Wed, Dec 31, 2014 at 2:26 PM, grad_student <alis...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, 

I have some large files from WGBS analysis, and I would prefer to avoid reading the files into R because it's taking too much memory and time. I'd like to find predefined genomic regions that are differentially methylated (i.e., promoters or 1kb tiles that are differentially methylated) using calculateDiffMeth. I have a file that looks like the example given in the guide after tileMethylCounts:

methylRaw object with 3 rows
--------------
chr start end strand coverage numCs numTs
1 chr21 9764001 9765000 * 24 3 21
2 chr21 9820001 9821000 * 13 0 13
3 chr21 9837001 9838000 * 11 0 11

I've generated this file outside of R. Is there a way to directly input this file as a MethylRaw object? I tried using the read function, but would need to modify the "end" column and the "strand" column? Is there a simple way to do this?

Alternatively, is there a way to read in a matrix directly into a methylBase object?

Thanks!
